sources.title: Injections
sources.what: Every HPLC injection of the study, one row per injection: exp, sample (0 is the first injection of an experiment), t_h (hours since the start, as the lab's files give it), pa_anti and pa_syn (peak areas of L-anti- and L-syn-phenylserine, instrument units). Raw: nothing is converted to a concentration.

sources.title: Conditions
sources.what: The conditions each experiment's file states, one row per experiment: exp, series (which of the lab's result files the experiment is from), temp_c, gly_m (mol/L), dmso_pct (vol.%), flow_ul_min (microlitres per minute). Blank where the files do not state it.

sources.title: Lab files
sources.what: The lab's own records: calibration, sample preparation, run sheet, instrument and materials.

sources.title: Reporting protocol
sources.what: The group's rules for blanks, yields, ratios, end points, outliers, rates and fits.

nodes.title: Experiment registry
nodes.what: 79 experiments in five process modes: two-phase batch (12), membrane (39), one-phase batch (3), flow (21), recycle (4). Each has its sampling plan.
hard: Flow and recycle experiments have no glycine in the conditions file (blank), and no temperature or DMSO either; flow_ul_min is blank for all four recycle runs -> a9 (glycine 0.45 mol/L for flow and recycle)

output.schema: CSV with the header exp,mode,temp_c,gly_m,dmso_pct,flow_ul_min,n_samples,final_t_h and one row per experiment (79 rows). mode is one of batch2p (two-phase batch), membrane, batch1p (one-phase batch), flow, recycle. temp_c (deg C), gly_m (initial glycine, mol/L), dmso_pct (vol.%) and flow_ul_min (microlitres per minute) are the experiment's conditions, left empty where the experiment has none; n_samples is its number of injections and final_t_h the hours of its last injection.

families.what: the process mode of each experiment
temperature, glycine, DMSO and flow rate of each experiment, empty ones included

nodes.title: Calibration
nodes.what: Which calibration converts each injection, and how.
hard: Experiment 1 was evaluated with an earlier calibration, through the origin -> a5
Only L-anti standards were run, so syn is quantified on the anti calibration -> a12

nodes.title: Dilution map

nodes.title: Kinetic model
nodes.what: One mechanistic model fitted jointly to every batch and membrane time course.
hard: Which mechanism to fit: irreversible, reversible aldol, or with enzyme decay; the choice changes every rate constant downstream -> Q2 (reversible aldol has the lowest joint SSE; decay is within 1.7 %)

output.schema: JSON object {"mechanism": "reversible", "ea_fixed_kj_mol": ..., "params": {"batch2p": {"kf30", "k2", "dmso_exp"}, "membrane": {...}}, "sse": {"batch2p", "membrane", "total"}, "rmse": sqrt(total sse / total points), "n_points": {"batch2p", "membrane"}}. mechanism is the mechanism you fitted: one of irreversible, reversible, decay. The model: p(t) = kf G0 / (kf + k2) (1 - exp(-(kf + k2) t)) for the total phenylserine concentration p (mmol/L), G0 = 1000 x the glycine concentration in mol/L, kf = kf30 exp(-Ea/R (1/T - 1/303.15)) exp(dmso_exp (DMSO - 25)/25) with T in kelvin, DMSO in vol.%, R = 8.314 J/(mol K) and Ea the membrane activation energy of x2, held fixed; kf30 (1/h), k2 (1/h) and dmso_exp are fitted separately for the two modes batch2p and membrane, by least squares on every accepted, non-blank sample of every two-phase batch and membrane experiment.

nodes.title: Residual review

nodes.title: Robustness
nodes.what: The optimum re-solved over a fixed bootstrap of experiments.
hard: The bootstrap is only comparable if the resampling is exactly the stated one: numpy RandomState(20261115), 200 draws of 51 -> definition in the schema

output.schema: JSON object {"n_boot": 200, "n_degenerate", "factor_choice": {"temp_c": {"lo", "hi", "interior"}, "dmso_pct": {...}, "gly_m": {...}}, "same_corner_share", "yield_ci": {"lo", "hi"}}. Resample the 51 two-phase batch and membrane experiments with replacement 200 times: for b in range(200), idx = numpy.random.RandomState(20261115).randint(0, 51, 51) drawn in sequence from one generator created once, the experiments taken in increasing experiment number. On each resample refit x3's yield surface (the same eight terms, ordinary least squares, numpy.linalg.lstsq) and re-solve z1's optimum with the same rules; a resample whose design matrix has rank below 8 is counted in n_degenerate and skipped. factor_choice gives, per factor, the share of the usable resamples whose optimum is at the lowest tested level (lo), the highest (hi), or strictly between (interior); same_corner_share is the share whose three choices equal z1's; yield_ci is the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles (numpy.percentile) of the optimum yield over the usable resamples.

facts.text: Calibration from the neat standards: PA = 1731.36 x c + 172.70, with c the injected concentration in mmol/L. A concentration is obtained by inverting it: c = (PA - 172.70) / 1731.36.
Samples were diluted 1:5 with water before injection, so the concentration in the reaction mixture is 5 times the injected one. This holds unless another note says otherwise.
Experiments 23 and 24 were diluted 1:10 instead, for every sample.
In experiments 21 and 22 only the 24 h sample was diluted 1:10; their other samples follow the usual dilution.
Experiment 1 was evaluated with the earlier calibration PA = 1755.1 x c, through the origin (c the injected concentration in mmol/L); its dilution still applies.
In experiments 59 to 61 the first sample was diluted 1:5 and every later sample 1:2.
Experiments 62 to 64 and 67 were injected undiluted: no dilution step at all.
In experiments 65 and 66 the first two samples were injected undiluted and the later ones diluted 1:5.
The flow and recycle experiments ran on 0.45 mol/L glycine.
The series with one aqueous phase (batch1p) was sampled on a 10 min grid below 2 h; its hours column is rounded, so the true time is the nearest multiple of 10 min.
The membrane module's channel volume is 243 microliters; the residence time is the volume divided by the flow rate.
Only L-anti standards were injected; the syn peak is quantified with the same calibration.
Column: Nucleosil Chiral-1 (Macherey-Nagel); mobile phase 0.5 mM CuSO4 in water at 1 mL/min.
Detection: UV-Vis at 200 nm, with the column held at 50 degrees C.
The HPLC system is an Agilent 1260; chromatograms are exported from OpenLab CDS to spreadsheets.
The membrane module uses a dialysis membrane with a 1 kDa cut-off.
The module ran with the enzyme and the cofactor PLP (pyridoxal phosphate) in the batch chamber.
For the flow runs the buffer was first saturated with benzaldehyde, then glycine and enzyme were dissolved in it.
The sample at time 0 is a blank: the lab sets both of its concentrations to zero instead of computing them from the calibration.
Yield is the percentage of the initial glycine that has become phenylserine: 100 x (c_anti + c_syn) / (1000 x c_glycine), with the concentrations in mmol/L and the glycine in mol/L.
The diastereomer ratio R is PA_syn / PA_anti, a ratio of the areas themselves; the concentrations are not used for it.
The end point of a batch or membrane experiment is its last valid sample taken at or before 6 h; later samples are not part of the protocol.
The steady state of a flow experiment is the mean of its samples 4 to 6, for concentrations and peak areas alike; its yield and ratio are computed from those means.

A sample taken at or before 6 h whose total peak area (anti + syn) is below 95 % of the highest total of the experiment's earlier valid samples is an outlier. Outliers are left out of end points, rates and fits.
The initial rate is the least-squares slope (free intercept) of the total concentration c_anti + c_syn against time, over the valid samples taken at or before 2 h, the blank included.
The rate constant k comes from c(t) = c_inf x (1 - exp(-k t)), fitted by least squares to the total concentration over the valid samples at or before 6 h, the blank included; c_inf is fitted too.

The activation energy is -R times the slope of ln k against 1/T, with T in kelvin (degrees C + 273.15) and R = 8.314 J/(mol K), by least squares through the mean k of each temperature; it is reported in kJ/mol.
The lab's reference group is the membrane experiments with 1.0 mol/L glycine and 25 vol.% DMSO.
The end point of a recycle experiment is its last sample, however late it was taken.
An experiment whose end-point yield is below 1 % is too flat to fit: it gets no initial rate and no fit.
The enzyme is L-threonine aldolase; the substrates are glycine and benzaldehyde.
In the first batch series benzaldehyde, which hardly dissolves in water, formed a second phase.
In the membrane-assisted series the dialysis membrane passively controls the transport of benzaldehyde into the aqueous phase.
The recycle runs pumped the reaction mixture back through the reactor at 10 mL/h.
The authors' tables end each flow block with an overall row; the lab does not use it.
DMSO is the co-solvent that keeps the substrates in solution.

decisions.question: How are repeated conditions pooled before batch and membrane runs are paired (x1)?
decisions.answer: Replicate runs at the same conditions are pooled by the mean of their yields before pairing, so each condition set gives one pair; only condition sets with both a two-phase batch and a membrane run are paired.
decisions.plausible_default: Pair every batch run with every membrane run at the same conditions (cost: 39 run pairs instead of 5 condition pairs, and a different weight for the replicated conditions).
decisions.source: ruling (G1 builder, 2026-11-15): replicates are the same experiment repeated; the mean is the standard pooling; flagged for the user
decisions.convention: Repeated runs at the same temperature, glycine and DMSO are pooled by the mean of their yields before the batch and membrane runs are paired, so each condition set gives one pair.

decisions.question: Which mechanism does the kinetic model fit: irreversible, reversible aldol, or with enzyme decay (x4)?
decisions.answer: Reversible aldol: the product forms from glycine at a rate kf and reverts at a rate k2, with benzaldehyde saturated (constant), first order in the remaining glycine; one set of constants per mode, the activation energy of kf held at x2's membrane value, and a DMSO factor.
decisions.plausible_default: Irreversible first-order formation (3.6e5 without a DMSO term, 5.3 times the reversible model's SSE) or reversible with enzyme decay (the closest rival, 1.7 % larger).
decisions.source: ruling (G1 builder, 2026-11-15): joint SSE over the accepted non-blank samples: reversible 6.78e4, decay 6.89e4 (both with DMSO terms), irreversible 3.60e5 (one constant per mode, no DMSO term); flagged for the user
decisions.convention: The kinetic model is the reversible aldol (formation from glycine, first order in the remaining glycine, and reversion), with benzaldehyde taken as saturated; the temperature dependence of the formation rate uses the membrane activation energy found in the Arrhenius step.

decisions.question: What temperature is assumed for the flow runs, which have none on file (y1)?
decisions.answer: The flow runs are taken at 20 degC and 25 vol.% DMSO.
decisions.plausible_default: Take the flow runs at the middle temperature, 30 degC (cost: the predicted conversions rise about 20 %; the data cannot tell the temperatures apart, rmse 0.030, 0.028, 0.026 at 20, 30 and 40 degC).
decisions.source: ruling (G1 builder, 2026-11-15): three of the four membrane runs at 0.45 mol/L and 25 vol.% DMSO were at 20 degC; flagged for the user
decisions.convention: The flow runs, which have no temperature on file, are taken to have run at 20 degC with 25 vol.% DMSO, the conditions of the membrane runs closest to them (0.45 mol/L glycine, 25 vol.% DMSO; the flow file's own title states 25 % DMSO).

decisions.question: Is the outlier screen applied to the flow runs?
decisions.answer: No. The screen is for the batch, membrane and recycle time courses; the early samples of a flow run are start-up and are not screened.
decisions.convention: The outlier screen is applied to the batch, membrane and recycle time courses. The early samples of a flow run are start-up and are never screened.
decisions.plausible_default: Apply the rule to every experiment (cost if taken: 33 flow samples rejected on top of the 4 real outliers).
decisions.source: the Pool reference's practice (series flow is exempt); not stated in the data set; flagged for the user

title: Enzyme aldol process: raw HPLC data to a process decision
intro: A research group studied the enzymatic aldol synthesis of L-phenylserine from glycine and benzaldehyde with the enzyme L-threonine aldolase, in five reactor arrangements, and published every HPLC peak area as an open data set. `data/injections.csv` holds the raw peak areas of 79 experiments (649 injections), `data/experiments.csv` the conditions the lab's result files state for each experiment, and `docs/` the lab's own records and reporting protocol. Nothing in the data files has been converted: the deliverables below rebuild the study's quantities step by step.

reserved.note: The lab's LIMS submission, `scripts/submit_to_lims.sh`, is for the lab to run after review: do not run it.

review_notes: Nodes after level 1 carry only the page's fields; their output paths, schemas and families are set when their stage is built.
